title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 25 | Week 12 vs. Washington Commanders
headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice Wednesday and Josh Johnson is being prepped to start vs. Washington; Jeremiyah Love's return from IR will be decided Monday.
summary: LaFleur said Carson Beck did not practice Wednesday because of his back. It is better than Tuesday, but the team is taking it one day at a time, and the staff is preparing Josh Johnson to start. LaFleur does not think the back will keep Beck out beyond this week, but he admitted that with a back you can never be sure. He said IR has not been discussed for Beck. Jon Gaines had a setback in his first 11-on-11 work and most likely will not play this week. Jeremiyah Love is doing well but is still inside his four-week IR window. The staff will decide Monday whether he returns for the Philadelphia game or whether they use the bye week for the extra recovery time. A new coach has taken over the defense, and LaFleur said changes will be tweaks rather than a wholesale overhaul, noting the defense is a 3-4 base. On offense, Johnson will work with the same group that played at Kansas City, so the unit should have some continuity this week. LaFleur called Jayden Daniels a stud and said Washington is playing good football. Thursday's Thanksgiving schedule is compressed, with a modified practice.

injuries.detail: Back issue flared up a second time. He did not practice Wednesday but will throw. LaFleur said he is better than Tuesday, does not expect him to miss more than this week, and says IR has not been discussed.
Ankle. He had a setback after returning to 11-on-11 work last week. LaFleur said he will most likely not be ready this week.
Still inside his four-week IR window but progressing well. The team will decide Monday whether he returns for Philadelphia or uses the bye week for extra time.
Limited at Wednesday's practice.
Captions say 'Maxx' will be limited on what is normally a rest day because of some tweaks. It is unclear whether this is Max Melton or Mack Wilson.
Veteran rest day, not a listed injury.
Veteran rest day.
Rest day.
Rest day.

signals.note: Beck's status is uncertain, and his back has flared up twice, so he is a risky start.
signals.quote: Better than yesterday. Hopefully better tomorrow.

signals.claim: Josh Johnson is being prepared to start at QB against Washington.
signals.note: Johnson is the likely starting QB if Beck cannot go, which affects the whole passing offense.
signals.quote: Yeah, yeah, that's what we're preparing for.

signals.claim: Arizona will decide Monday whether Love returns from IR for the Philadelphia game or uses the bye week for the extra recovery time.
signals.note: Love is progressing, but his return is not locked in for the next game.
signals.quote: obviously he's still in his four week window there on IR

signals.claim: Gaines will most likely miss Sunday's game after a setback.
signals.note: The offensive line stays thin, which could hurt the offense's pass protection.
signals.quote: Uh, most likely no.

topics.detail: A new coach has taken over the defense. LaFleur declined to give specifics but said there will be no wholesale scheme change with six weeks left, only tweaks. The front stays a 3-4. Who calls plays and from where can be decided as late as Sunday.

The group that played at Kansas City will largely play Sunday. LaFleur is encouraged that Johnson now has a full week to work with them, after only a Friday practice and a Saturday walk-through last week.
Wednesday ends with extra meetings, and Thursday starts at 7 a.m. with a modified, not fully padded practice. Players are done by noon. The team will use all 14 allowed padded practices this season.
LaFleur called Jayden Daniels a stud and said Washington's record understates how talented the team is. Its defense has built continuity over the last month after early injuries up front.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski on Sunday's Week 12 matchup against Vikings | Press Conference
headline: Falcons are on a short Thanksgiving-week prep for Minnesota. James Pearce Jr. (back) is improving and will be at practice, and Stefanski declined to say which other injured players will be available.
summary: Stefanski opened the Week 12 prep by praising the Vikings, their staff and the road environment. He called Brian Flores' defense the league leader in pressure rate, and said its versatile players and shifting looks make blocking assignments hard to identify. He said the bye-week self-scout gave the coaches things to adjust, but the players will only get a few high-level action items. On Michael Penix Jr. he refused to single out the quarterback. He said the offense's scoring drop-off belongs to every player and coach, and that all of them need more consistency. He said an unnamed coach, apparently the play-caller, will work on the field instead of up top, and that this person is comfortable doing either. On health, he said players are getting better and some will be held out of practice today while the team watches rehab and field work. James Pearce Jr. is dealing with a back issue and is getting better, and Stefanski confirmed he is aware of a social media post about an agreement Pearce was supposed to be following but gave no detail. He also talked about his Thanksgiving routine, the former Falcons quarterback Kirk (not on the roster) now running Minnesota's offense, and his admiration for Vikings safety Harrison Smith.

injuries.detail: Back issue. Stefanski had no formal update but said he is getting better and will be at practice today.

signals.claim: James Pearce will be at practice today while his back issue improves.
signals.note: The pass rusher's back issue is improving but his Sunday availability is not confirmed, so monitor practice reports.
signals.quote: no update getting better though

signals.note: Stefanski acknowledged an off-field issue (a social media post about an agreement) but gave no details, so there is some uncertainty around Pearce.
signals.quote: I'm aware we've spoken to James, but I don't have much more to add

signals.note: Stefanski would not single out the quarterback for the recent scoring decline and said the whole offense needs more consistency, so the quarterback's volatility remains a concern.
signals.quote: we just have not been consistent enough

topics.detail: Stefanski said Brian Flores' unit has by far the NFL's highest pressure rate, uses versatile players who can rush or drop into coverage, and changes its looks to complicate blocking assignments. He called it schematically sound with great players at every level.

Kirk is back in a system he already knows, which Stefanski said looks seamless and natural. Stefanski downplayed the extra familiarity with Atlanta's scheme as the usual 'they know that we know' dynamic, and said the Falcons will change calls and signals.
The staff used the bye week for a deep self-scout and found adjustments. Stefanski said players will get only high-level action items so they can play fast.

Last week the play-caller (apparently Tommy) was moved from the booth to the field and will be on the field again Sunday. Stefanski said he is comfortable calling plays from either spot and called the change part of a search for consistency.
Stefanski said everyone is getting better, but some players will be held out of practice today to see how they progress. Final decisions depend on rehab and field work today and tomorrow.
The team will meet and practice Thursday morning, then give players and coaches the afternoon off. Stefanski said the short week is not a bigger challenge.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Injury Updates
headline: Derrick Henry was put back in concussion protocol after brief symptoms late in the game, but Minter expects him to play vs. Houston; Marlon Humphrey, Nnamdi Madubuike and Jaylinn Hawkins are all unresolved.
summary: Minter opened by saying Derrick Henry had a couple of brief concussion symptoms near the end of the last game. He tested clear, but the team put him back in protocol to be safe. Henry would have been limited at Wednesday's practice, and Minter expects him back for Houston. Marlon Humphrey is back in meetings and practice, but his Sunday status is undetermined and will depend on how the week goes. Nnamdi Madubuike and Jaylinn Hawkins are both still working through unspecified issues, and Hawkins did not practice. The punt return job is not settled, and the team will decide by the end of the week. Minter said Jacoby Brissett is comfortable with the offense, apart from normal early-week adjustment when older plays return. He praised the offensive line for its continuity and run-game identity. He also described Justice Hill as a change-of-pace runner who has made plays in the last couple of games.

injuries.detail: Brief concussion symptoms late in the last game. He tested cleared but was put back in protocol, would have been limited Wednesday, and is expected to return.
Back in meetings and practice, but Minter called Sunday's availability undetermined and said it depends on how the week goes. He denied it was about performance.
Did not practice Wednesday and was also out last week. Minter said only that he is still working through some stuff.
Still working through an unspecified issue, not described as concussion-related. The team will reassess closer to the end of the week.

signals.claim: Henry will clear the concussion protocol and play Sunday vs. Houston.
signals.note: Henry is in the concussion protocol, so his Sunday availability depends on clearing it, even though the coach expects him back.
signals.quote: We do expect him to be back

signals.claim: Humphrey's availability for Sunday will be decided later in the week.
signals.note: IDP managers should wait for the practice reports, because Minter would not commit to him playing.
signals.quote: see how the week goes

signals.note: He missed practice for a second straight week and the coach gave no detail, so his Sunday status is a concern.
signals.quote: working through some stuff

signals.claim: Madubuike's status will be clearer toward the end of the week.
signals.note: The coach gave no timeline, so check the later injury reports before setting IDP lineups.
signals.quote: still working through some stuff

signals.claim: Brissett will be prepared for Sunday's game plan despite re-learning some older plays.
signals.note: The coach downplayed concerns about Brissett's grasp of the playbook, so he looks set to play.
signals.quote: I don't think going into a game he's ever uncomfortable with what we're doing.

signals.claim: Hill will continue as the change-of-pace back behind Henry.
signals.note: Hill has made plays and scored recently, but his role is a complement to Henry, so his value rises if Henry misses time.
signals.quote: he's brought some juice, he's made some plays

topics.detail: Several players fielded punts last game. Minter says the team has a pretty good idea of who it wants but will decide by the end of the week.
Minter liked the line's continuity since Cam Jurgens returned and its run-game identity last game. He said early runs may gain only 2-3 yards but the line adjusts to how the defense plays them.

A player Minter called David made his debut with roughly 20-22 snaps. Minter said offensive linemen had urged the staff to give him a shot, and that he has stood out in practice for 3-4 weeks. The name does not match the roster, so he is not named in the signals.
Minter said Henry means everything to the team and offense, and that he asks for more on his own shoulders when things aren't working.

title: Dave Canales: 'We've got to stay aggressive'
headline: Jonathon Brooks' practice window is open and he's 'looked really good'; Tetairoa McMillan's foot soreness isn't a serious concern ahead of Monday night at Tampa Bay.
summary: Canales said the Panthers open a player's practice window once he is healthy and in good enough shape to take on full practice reps. That applied to Brooks this week. The caption names are garbled here, and the coach's answers about the running back room and the Monday-night deadline point to Brooks. Brooks is described as doing everything he can to show he's ready, but the team is weighing where he fits on game day. A roster decision comes right after the Monday night game if he isn't activated this week. McMillan finished Sunday's game on a sore foot, and Canales is optimistic and not seriously worried, though the team is also looking to give veterans some rest. The full injury report arrives Thursday, with Thanksgiving off and practice resuming Friday. Canales praised Bucky Irving's patience and vision and stressed containing Baker Mayfield's scrambling. He said the run defense under Todd Wash relies on aggressive linemen, active linebackers and everyone running to the ball. On offense he wants to stay aggressive and on schedule against Todd Bowles' top-five run defense, and he credited the improved pass protection, including rookie Monroe Freeling. He also explained that the multi-tight-end usage comes from the attention McMillan draws and the speed of Darren Waller.

injuries.detail: Finished Sunday's game on a sore foot (not an ankle). Canales is optimistic and 'not seriously concerned', and the team will ease him back gradually.
His practice window was opened this week and he has looked really good. He is listed questionable with a groin issue, and a roster decision is due after Monday night if he isn't activated this week.
Asked about alongside McMillan, but Canales only addressed McMillan and gave no specific update on Jones.

signals.note: Brooks may return to a backfield that Chuba Hubbard leads and Trevor Etienne contributes to, but his game-day role is still undecided.
signals.quote: He's looked really good this week.

signals.note: His return duties help secure his roster spot and bring a small amount of return-yardage upside.
signals.quote: Trevor's handling dual return responsibilities with punt and kick return.

signals.note: His speed and flexible alignment keep him involved in a multi-tight-end offense, though he is listed questionable with a knee issue.
signals.quote: getting into 11 personnel looks with Darren Waller basically as your third wide receiver

signals.claim: Pass protection and quick ball release will continue to improve, giving Young more time.
signals.note: Better protection and rhythm throws should help Young's efficiency against a Tampa Bay defense that sacked him five times last meeting.
signals.quote: the ball coming out early.

signals.claim: Freeling will keep starting and improving on the offensive line.
signals.note: The rookie's growth is part of why pass protection has improved.
signals.quote: a guy like Monroe, a rookie player who just continues to get better every week

topics.topic: Opponent: Bucky Irving and the run game
topics.detail: Canales praised Irving's patience and vision in the new Tampa Bay scheme. He noted Detroit limited him, with one 80-yard run called back for holding, and said the Panthers are building their response around Irving's run styles.

The emphasis is correct alignments, being in your gap, aggressive disruption up front and quickly activating linebackers. That breaks double-teams and frees Derrick Brown for one-on-one blocks, with everyone running to the ball.
Mayfield extends plays and escapes arm tackles, which helps his third-down efficiency and his off-schedule plays. Canales wants defenders to tackle low, keep their legs moving and contain him.

Canales called Tampa Bay a top-five run defense and said Carolina must run efficiently to avoid third-and-longs, where Bowles gets aggressive. He wants to stay aggressive, stay on schedule and attack the second level against blitzes.

Canales said the multi-tight-end approach works because defenses focus on McMillan, which opens space for others. Waller, Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans add speed and versatility, and the Panthers mix run and play-action looks.
Christensen's window was opened when the offensive line was banged up, but he reverted to IR without being activated. The line is now healthy and deep, so the team didn't need to activate him.
Practice was cold, wet and windy, which Canales saw as useful with rain possible Monday in Tampa. The team is off Thursday for Thanksgiving and returns Friday.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Week 11, Previews Week 12 Against Saints | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Dalton Risner is day-to-day for Sunday vs. the Saints, Shemar Stewart and Cedric Johnson are set for more DL snaps, and rookies Colbie Young and Jack Endries drew praise.
summary: Taylor called the loss to Washington disappointing and said both phases could have been cleaner. He defended going for the win with a pass on the final possession and put the blame for the failed third downs, including the last-play sack, on himself. Dalton Risner is day-to-day and Bryan Cook finished the game and should be fine, though Taylor cautioned against reading into today's walkthrough. Taylor said the run game needs to give more good opportunities, and he blamed that on everyone rather than the running backs. He said the offense will be "whoever we need to be" each week, whether that means leaning on the run or the pass. He praised rookies Colbie Young, who scored his first touchdown, and Jack Endries. He said the defensive line will rotate a bit more, with Shemar Stewart and Cedric Johnson mixed in, and called Stewart one of four players in the mix behind the two starters. He called New Orleans a talented, well-coached team with a dangerous front and a quarterback he likes, and said his team is glad to have a short week to bounce back.

injuries.detail: Taylor said he is day-to-day and they'll see where he is by Sunday. Today is a walkthrough only.
Possibly limited in the walkthrough, but he finished Sunday's game. Taylor said he feels pretty good about it.

signals.claim: Young will keep earning opportunities in the passing game after scoring his first touchdown.
signals.note: Young is earning the coach's trust as a rookie pass-catcher, which makes him a depth stash with touchdown upside.
signals.quote: when you get your opportunity, you take advantage of it

signals.claim: Endries is being pleasing as a rookie who makes plays when he gets the ball.
signals.note: Taylor praised him alongside Young, but no specific increase in role was promised.
signals.quote: I've been pleased with those two rookies.

signals.claim: Stewart will get more defensive line snaps in the rotation; he is one of four players in the mix behind two starters.
signals.note: Stewart sees a modest snap bump, but he is not a starter yet, so IDP value is limited.
signals.quote: find some opportunities for Shemar and Cedric to get in there and mix it in

signals.claim: Johnson will be mixed into the defensive line rotation more.
signals.note: Expect more snaps for Johnson, though the rotation is still described loosely.
signals.quote: we'll, we'll rotate those guys a little more.

signals.claim: Risner's availability for Sunday's game will be decided day to day.
signals.note: Offensive line depth could be affected if he can't play.
signals.quote: He'll be day to day.

signals.claim: Cook finished Sunday's game and is progressing each day.
signals.note: He is likely fine for Sunday, but his practice participation is worth tracking.
signals.quote: right now I feel pretty good about it.

topics.detail: Taylor said he wanted to put the ball in Joe Burrow's hands and try for a first down to win with a field goal. He said the outcome would have been the same either way and that he could have given the offense a better chance on the third-down sack.

Taylor said the run game needs to produce more but it is not an indictment of the running backs. He said efficiency and staying on schedule matter more than explosive plays, and that the offense will lean on whichever phase works.

Taylor said the team reviewed illegal-formation clock runoff scenarios on Saturday because they had lined up illegally vs. the Steelers. He said he has not heard back from the league about the Washington play.
Taylor praised Chase Young, the Saints' linebackers, their quarterback and a returning player named Tyson. He said the Saints' record doesn't show up on tape and they will come in to battle.
Tomorrow's practice is condensed with no break between walkthrough and practice, and meetings shift to Friday. Players are released after practice.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Will Anderson Jr.’s Dominance & Ravens | Full Q&A
headline: Ryans offered little fantasy news: Marvin Harrison Jr. is back at practice with no expectations set, Woody Marks is described as on his way back, and the Texans face a Ravens offense built on quick timing throws.
summary: Ryans opened by praising Will Anderson Jr., the AFC Defensive Player of the Week, saying his impact goes beyond the stat sheet because he sets the edge and pressures quarterbacks, which helps teammates make plays. Asked about the run game with Woody Marks on his way back, he spoke only in general terms about execution and finishing blocks, with no specifics on backfield usage. He said Marvin Harrison Jr. was in his first practice back, with no expectations beyond executing his assignments. He praised Jadeveon Clowney as a complete player, citing his run-game edge-setting on the first play against the Colts. He called Calen Bullock a true ballhawk who has had few interceptions this year and said the corners are knocking away balls that would have been his. On Baltimore, he called Lamar Jackson's timing and rhythm a major challenge, noted that Zay Flowers can turn short catches into explosive plays, and said the Ravens' outside zone run scheme won't change whether Derrick Henry (in concussion protocol) or Justice Hill plays. He also said the team is focused solely on winning each week and gave the players only a short Thanksgiving break.

injuries.detail: Took part in his first practice back, though the injury report lists him as out with a hamstring injury. Ryans said he has no expectations for him beyond executing.
A reporter described him as on his way back, and Ryans did not dispute it. The injury report lists him as out with a concussion.

signals.claim: Anderson will keep dominating as an edge rusher and run defender, with more to come this season.
signals.note: He is an elite IDP asset who is producing both on and off the stat sheet.
signals.quote: There's even more in store for him, so let's keep it going.

signals.claim: Clowney will keep improving as both a pass rusher and a run defender.
signals.note: Ryans called him productive and a complete player, which supports his IDP value.
signals.quote: Clowney has continued to improve each and every game.

signals.claim: Bullock is expected to get more chances for interceptions as the deep middle-of-the-field safety.
signals.note: He has only one interception this season, so positive turnover regression is possible for IDP.
signals.quote: He's a true ballhawk. That hasn't changed.

signals.claim: Harrison is returning to practice, but Ryans set no expectations for his role.
signals.note: His readiness for Sunday is unclear and he is listed as out, so avoid counting on him.
signals.quote: No expectations for Marvin.

signals.claim: Marks is on his way back from a concussion, but no return timeline was given.
signals.note: Ryans gave no workload details, so the backfield split with David Montgomery is unclear.

topics.detail: Lamar Jackson is a veteran who plays on time, so Houston's coverage drops need to be precise, and the defense must tackle well on quick throws to Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews.
Baltimore runs outside zone no matter whether Derrick Henry (concussion protocol) or Justice Hill carries the ball. Houston must set the edge and close on cutbacks.
Ryans said the team is focused only on winning each week and is not following the standings.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Giants
headline: Anthony Richardson gets his opportunity at QB with Jonathan Taylor in the backfield, DJ Giddens steps in as RB2 with Seth McGowan down, and Alec Pierce will not practice this week.
summary: Steichen is looking forward to hosting a Giants team he says is playing good ball, with a strong pass-rushing D-line, a good tight end and a hard-running Scotty. The Colts opened Cam Taylor-Britt's practice window and will see how his week goes. Caden Curry is on IR with a torn wrist ligament that needed a procedure, so he is done for the season. Steichen praised Anthony Richardson for his work on the scout team and his preparation as a backup, and said he is excited for his opportunity. He expects the offense to be built around Richardson and Jonathan Taylor as two run threats, as it was when they shared the field before. Seth McGowan is down, and Steichen called it very unfortunate. DJ Giddens will step into the No. 2 back role, and Steichen said they will work through his workload this week. Alec Pierce will not practice this week, and no decision has been made on him because they want him 100% healthy. The team is also bringing in veteran QB Shane Buechele and will get him up to speed, with no word on whether he practices this week.

injuries.detail: Ligament tear in his wrist, had a procedure, and will miss the rest of the season.
The Colts opened his practice window. How the week goes will determine his next step.
He will not practice this week. No determination has been made, and the team wants him 100% healthy before he returns. He has been rehabbing since getting hurt in the Kansas City game.
Coach said he is 'down' and called it very unfortunate, with no specifics on the injury or timeline. The video description says he is set to miss some time.

In response to a question about a player 'still just rehabbing' (the name was garbled in the captions), Steichen said he will be out at practice this week and they will see how the week progresses. The player is unclear.

signals.claim: Richardson will get his opportunity to play quarterback this week against the Giants.
signals.note: Richardson is getting his chance at QB after a long wait, and Steichen praised his preparation.
signals.quote: I'm really excited for him.

signals.claim: The game plan will be built around Taylor and Richardson both as run threats, and Taylor should absorb work with McGowan down.
signals.note: A run-heavy plan with a mobile QB and McGowan out points to a strong workload for Taylor.
signals.quote: there are two threats to run the football

signals.claim: Giddens will be the No. 2 RB with McGowan out, though his workload is still to be determined.
signals.note: He steps into the backup RB role, but Steichen did not commit to a McGowan-sized workload.
signals.quote: D.J. has done some good things in practice

signals.claim: McGowan will be unavailable while he is down with an injury.
signals.note: McGowan had been more productive than Taylor in the stretch where they split work, and he is now out of the lineup.
signals.quote: obviously very unfortunate what happened to Seth

signals.claim: Pierce will not practice this week, and the team has not decided on his return.
signals.note: No practice this week makes his availability for the Giants game doubtful.
signals.quote: we want to make sure he's 100% healthy

signals.claim: Taylor-Britt's practice window is open, and the team will decide on his return based on how the week goes.
signals.note: A possible return for IDP and defensive-matchup purposes; watch his practice participation.

topics.detail: Steichen said the Giants are playing really good ball, with a D-line that rushes the passer well. He also pointed to their skill players, a good tight end and a hard-running Scotty.

The team made a lot of roster moves in the last couple of days, including signing veteran QB Shane Buechele, who has played in Kansas City and Buffalo. Steichen said they will get him up to speed this week and see where it goes.
Steichen praised his high level of play on defense and special teams and expects him to attack his rehab and be ready in the offseason.

title: Liam Coen Talks Game-Planning for Titans, Focus on Being Fundamentally Sharp | Press Conference
headline: Coen is simplifying the offense after the Giants loss, leaning on his tight ends, and managing Bhayshul Tuten's ankle, which could mean more work for LeQuint Allen Jr.
summary: Coen said the offense is going back to basics after a poor Sunday night loss to the Giants. That means cutting volume, motions and moving parts so players can play freely. He admitted he had a feeling beforehand that there was too much volume and should have listened to it. The Jaguars face the Titans for the second time in three weeks. He called that 'interesting' and said the focus is fundamentals and self-scouting, especially the red zone, where they struggled against Tennessee. He praised the tight end group for allowing multiple personnel groupings and for Brenton Strange's moves between the backfield and the core. He said the game script against the Giants got out of balance and he expects the tight ends to help a lot this week. On the Titans, he praised Cam Ward's confidence and scrambling, Tony Pollard's workload, Carnell Tate's return, and the interior defensive linemen, who can make running up the middle hard. On the backfield, he said Tuten's health is the priority and that LeQuint Allen Jr. has improved his detail and could get more work depending on Tuten's workload. He also noted that 56 players came in on an off day, and that a veteran named Patrick, who was hurt early, was getting his practice window opened to add depth and competition.

injuries.detail: Listed limited with an ankle injury. Coen said getting him healthy is the top priority and that his workload this week is being managed.
Coen discussed a veteran named Patrick who was hurt early and is now being opened up in practice. He is about 305 pounds and feels strong. The name could not be matched to the roster with confidence.

signals.claim: Strange will be moved around between the core and the backfield and be a big part of the game plan against Tennessee.
signals.note: Coen highlighted Strange's versatile alignment and expects the tight ends to be a big help after the game script got away from the offense.
signals.quote: move them out of the core and into the backfield and vice versa

signals.claim: Koziol has a defined role in the multiple tight end groupings.
signals.note: Coen said the tight ends each do different things well, but he gave no specifics on Koziol's snaps.
signals.quote: they all have a role

signals.claim: Allen may see more touches this week depending on Tuten's workload.
signals.note: Coen said Allen's improved detail puts him in a position to take on more work, but Allen is also limited with a hamstring injury.
signals.quote: Laquinton, I think has improved his detail over the last few weeks

signals.claim: Tuten's workload is being managed this week as he works back to full health.
signals.note: Coen praised Tuten's speed and tackle-breaking but said health is the priority, which puts his Week 12 volume in doubt.
signals.quote: got to get him healthy though. Like we have to get him feeling better.

topics.detail: The offense is trimming volume, motions and indicators to simplify the operation after the Giants loss. Coen blamed himself for ignoring his intuition that there was too much volume.
This is the second meeting in three weeks. The focus is fundamentals and self-scouting, especially the red zone, where the Jaguars struggled in the first Tennessee game.
Coen praised Cam Ward's growth, confidence and fourth-down scrambling. He also praised Tony Pollard's workload, a big offensive line, and the return of receiver Carnell Tate.
Coen said interior defenders like John Franklin-Myers make running up the middle difficult. He expects to pick his spots between inside and outside runs and between zone and gap schemes.
Coen hopes the run defense has improved with the added interior defensive linemen and the sure tackling behind them. He named Antonio Johnson among the back-end tacklers.
56 players came in on an off day after the loss, which Coen called rare. He credited leaders such as Josh Hines-Allen for that culture.

title: Jim Harbaugh on DJ Uiagalelei’s Development and Preparing for the Patriots
headline: Justin Herbert is in concussion protocol and the Chargers aren't saying whether he can play, so DJ Uiagalelei is taking first-team reps. Njoku, Keaton Mitchell and Brenen Thompson also sat out practice.
summary: Harbaugh opened by praising the Patriots on both sides of the ball. He called their offense mobile and good downfield, with a very good run game and playmakers. He called the defense excellent against the run, strong on the edge, inside and at linebacker, and very good in coverage. He confirmed Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol and refused several times to discuss whether Herbert could play Sunday, calling it a doctor-driven decision. A long list of players did not practice, including Herbert, David Njoku, Brenen Thompson, Keaton Mitchell and several defenders, and Teair Tart and Khalil Mack were given rest days. With about 10-11 players out, practice volume is down, and the backups are getting what he calls opportunity-squad reps. DJ Uiagalelei is expected to work with the first team, which Harbaugh called valuable 'time on task'. He said Uiagalelei has already handled game situations well, has grown a lot, and that the play-calling would have some nuance with him in the lineup. On his job security, Harbaugh said scrutiny is fair and his focus is narrowly on winning the next game.

title: Klint Kubiak: 'Confidence comes from demonstrated performance'
headline: Brock Bowers (ankle) and Tonka Hemingway were limited, and Kubiak is optimistic both play Sunday night at Cleveland; Adam Butler and Tim Keenan did not practice.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Adam Butler (apparently, from 'A B') and Tim Keenan did not practice, while Brock Bowers and Tonka Hemingway were limited. He is optimistic that both Bowers and Hemingway can play Sunday night. He was asked whether the back half of the season could affect Bowers' availability and said any healthy player will be on the field. He said rookie QB Fernando Mendoza is processing faster with repetition, calling his last two games 'solid' while stressing that he must keep improving and that the whole team shares the load. He gave credit to the offensive line and to Denver for the batted passes and pass-protection issues. He said the run game's success against a good defense builds confidence. On the defensive tackle group, he said the team has young players it believes in and brought a guy onto the practice squad. He declined to say who will get the most corner reps, but praised Darien Porter and Hezekiah Masses and the room as a whole. He was also glowing about Nakobe Dean, whom he called intelligent, physical, and a positive influence on teammates. The game is a flexed Sunday night primetime contest in the elements against Cleveland, which he said finishes games better than anyone.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Preparing for Falcons, Confidence in Defense & Kirk Cousins’ Leadership
headline: Kirk Cousins is Minnesota's quarterback and gets praise heading home vs. ATL, but Darrisaw, Addison, Redmond, Rodgers and Harrison Smith are all estimated DNPs on a walkthrough day.
summary: O'Connell opened with Thanksgiving wishes and said the team had plenty of energy after Sunday's loss to the Niners. He called Atlanta a rested, talented and physical team, praising the Falcons' front and their habit of rotating pass rushers. The estimated DNPs today are Jordan Addison, Christian Darrisaw, Jalen Redmond (a sore ankle), Isaiah Rodgers and Harrison Smith. Today was walkthrough only, with full practices the next two days, and he said most of these players are being worked back with the hope of seeing where they stand by the end of the week. On a shoulder injury, which appears to be Darrisaw's, he said it is early to tell but he has no long-term fears, and he was very hopeful on Smith's soreness. He was encouraged by Cousins' pre-snap command, communication and third-down conversions (about 50% since Cousins took over), and is excited to see him use cadence at home. He said pass protection is about the whole offense, including backs and timing, and not just the line, especially against a high-pressure Falcons defense. He also defined a good run game by early-down consistency and explosives over 10 yards, and praised Bijan Robinson's vision as the best of any back.

title: Kellen Moore previews Bengals game | Saints vs. Bengals 2026 NFL Week 12
headline: TE Juwan Johnson did not practice Wednesday (hamstring, wrist), while Taliese Fuaga, Erik McCoy and Asim Richards were limited as possible offensive line returns. Coach Moore praised Chris Olave, Jordyn Tyson and Alvin Kamara's red-zone role.
summary: Moore opened with the Wednesday injury report. Juwan Johnson did not practice with a hamstring and a wrist issue. David Edwards (hamstring), Taliese Fuaga (knee), Erik McCoy (biceps), Asim Richards (knee) and Pete Werner (hamstring) were limited, and Martin Emerson practiced fully after his concussion. He was noncommittal on Fuaga and McCoy, saying they are good players the team would love to have but that this week will take its course. He gave a vague 'day to day' answer on a second injury, and the player he meant is unclear. On offense he praised Chris Olave's third-down work and Jordyn Tyson's development. He said Alvin Kamara's red-zone role grew as the season went on, in both the pass and run games. Tyler Shough has some plays to clean up, such as pump fakes and frenetic pocket movement, but Moore said he played good football and gave the team a chance. Moore wants more tempo offense but says it has to be earned with first downs, and he admits the team needs to score more. On defense he said the interior linemen (Khristian Boyd, Colby Wooden) have improved against the run, Chase Young and Carl Granderson are relentless, and Kool-Aid McKinstry is playing tight, physical coverage ahead of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. He called Cincinnati's offense one of the league's best and said Dexter Lawrence has had a huge impact on its defense.

title: Coach John Harbaugh previews Week 12 vs. Colts
headline: Andru Phillips and Shelby Harris missed practice with illness, and one more player was seen on the side with a minor issue; Harbaugh is praising the run-defense depth, including Dawuane Smoot.
summary: Harbaugh opened with Thanksgiving talk and said practice was sharp ahead of Sunday's game at Indianapolis. He called Colts QB Anthony Richardson a rare athlete and arm talent who is hard to prepare for. The Giants have about 700 plays of his NFL tape, but they can't know which plays the Colts will build around him. He praised Jonathan Taylor as one of the league's top backs, a slashing, crease-hitting runner who also catches and pass-protects. He expects Indianapolis, ranked 8th in rushing, to lean on the downhill run game, quarterback runs and play-action. On injuries, Andru Phillips and Shelby Harris were out with illness. Someone else was seen on the side with a minor issue, called day-to-day and expected to be fine for the game, but the transcript doesn't make clear who. Harbaugh credited the improved run defense to gap discipline, the veteran tackles, depth players, edge-setting and discipline against play action. He singled out Dawuane Smoot as disruptive after a few weeks of getting his football legs back, and said CJ Okoye played well last week. He also praised Dennard Wilson's consistent defensive system and accountability.

headline: Sirianni says Dallas Goedert is in every game plan and Makai Lemon will be a big piece against the Cowboys, but he made no concrete target or snap commitments.
summary: Before the Thanksgiving game at Dallas, Sirianni spoke with a lot of respect for the Cowboys and stressed staying locked in on a big stage. He sidestepped a question about the offense's third-quarter scoring problem and answered with generalities about the matchup. Asked why Dallas Goedert isn't targeted more, he said a lack of targets doesn't mean Goedert wasn't the first read. He said the offense needs to be more efficient on third down and sustain drives, which would raise touches for everyone. He added that Goedert is one of the first players he thinks of in the pass game, and that the intent is to get the ball to Goedert, DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley. On Makai Lemon, who had a bigger role while Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were out, he said Lemon will be a big piece against Dallas' man and zone looks, without discussing a split of targets. He called Barkley one of the team's best leaders for three years. He praised the Cowboys' balanced offense (run game, two dynamic receivers, Fournette, Dak Prescott) and said the run scheme reflects Clayton Adams' influence. He also praised kicker Jake Elliott as clutch and said his confidence in him is extremely high.

Abraham Lucas is out with an ankle injury that Macdonald put at days to weeks. Quenton Nelson is probably not going to make the game and has had no setback in his knee recovery, though the team is hopeful for next week. Leonard Williams and Anthony Bradford are expected to be limited in practice. Josh Jones will slide over to right tackle, and Macdonald expects no drop-off from him. On defense, he said Mike Morris is at his best on the edge and will be needed down the stretch. He also said Rylie Mills and Connor O'Toole have gained confidence from extra reps, which lets the staff keep the defensive rotation going. On the 49ers, he praised their offense and the additions of Keenan Allen and Mike Evans. He said Brock Purdy is not practicing and his status is uncertain, with Mac Jones a possibility, and stressed sticking to Seattle's own process.

Macdonald avoids comparing this game to the first meeting with the 49ers. He wants Seattle to keep improving its process, including its run game, and said it has been improving over the last few weeks.

title: Shanahan, Morris Talk Seahawks Prep, Injury Updates Ahead of Week 12
headline: Brock Purdy (ankle) missed Wednesday practice and is day to day for Seattle. Mike Evans remains on a managed Achilles plan, and Fred Warner's partner Dre Greenlaw (neck) also sat out.
summary: Shanahan opened with the injury report: Purdy hurt his ankle in the second quarter Sunday and could not practice. Shanahan said it is not a high ankle sprain, but he is concerned and it is day to day. Mike Evans sat out with Achilles tendinitis, and Shanahan said he will keep managing it, with no Wednesday practices and limited snaps in games. Colton McKivitz is out, so a swing tackle moves into the lineup. Shanahan praised that player's play against Minnesota but did not name him in the captions. Kaelon Black's complementary role behind Christian McCaffrey was discussed, and Shanahan said it is deliberate and McCaffrey accepts it. He was glowing about Keenan Allen and Evans together against Seattle's two-shell defense. DC Raheem Morris said Garret Wallow and Jaden Dugger stepped in well with Dre Greenlaw out. He also previewed Seattle's run game and backs, saying the offense is essentially unchanged with Drew Lock. Brandin Cooks was released and has joined Washington.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury from the second quarter Sunday. Did not practice Wednesday. Not a high ankle sprain, but day to day, and Shanahan said he is concerned.
Achilles tendinitis. Did not practice Wednesday, which is the usual management plan. He will keep being managed in games.
Neck, described as nerve-related and on and off. Did not practice Wednesday. Shanahan felt better about him this week than last.
Starting right tackle lost, ending the run of ten games with the same starting five. A swing tackle stepped in Sunday night.
Knee/foot. Did not practice.
Groin. Did not practice.
Illness. Limited in practice. The captions say 'Carter', so the name is a best guess.
Foot. Appears to be the 'Demo' limited on the report, though that is a best guess from the captions.
Shoulder/neck. Limited in practice.

signals.claim: Purdy's availability for Sunday vs. Seattle is uncertain and depends on how the ankle responds this week.
signals.note: A QB1 with a day-to-day ankle makes his status and the rest of the passing game a lineup risk until he practices.
signals.quote: he can't go today. It's always a possibility.

signals.claim: Evans will keep being managed for the rest of the year, with no Wednesday practices and snaps limited in games.
signals.note: Expect a capped snap share even when he plays, which adds some week-to-week variance.
signals.quote: he probably would never practice Wednesdays regardless.

signals.claim: Allen and Evans will play together as starting receivers against Seattle's two-shell defense.
signals.note: Allen is a trusted starter alongside Evans, which helps against Seattle's tight coverage.
signals.quote: having another guy out there makes it makes your percentages a lot higher

signals.claim: McCaffrey will keep sharing carries with a complementary back rather than playing every snap.
signals.note: The workload split caps his snap share even though he is producing at a high level.

signals.claim: Black will keep a complementary role behind McCaffrey by design.
signals.note: A steady change-of-pace role has some flex appeal, with upside if McCaffrey is rested. The name is a best guess from the captions ('Calan'/'Kaitlyn').
signals.quote: I always tell him that's what I'm trying to do.

signals.claim: Wallow played well next to Fred Warner in place of the injured Dre Greenlaw and can be trusted in any situation.
signals.note: He is the first fill-in for Greenlaw, so he has IDP value if Greenlaw misses time.
signals.quote: he's one of those guys that can go out there and play in any situation.

signals.claim: Dugger also played well in the linebacker rotation without Greenlaw.
signals.note: He is depth behind Warner and Wallow and may see snaps again if Greenlaw is out.

signals.claim: Greenlaw's neck issue is nerve-related and has been on and off, so his Sunday availability is uncertain.
signals.note: If he is out, Wallow and Dugger take his snaps.
signals.quote: I think it's more nerve stuff which come and go.

topics.detail: Shanahan said losing McKivitz ended the run of ten games with the same starting five. A swing tackle, whom Shanahan said was brought in to be a capable starter, played well Sunday night against Minnesota. The player's name was not clear in the captions.
Shanahan said Seattle is a heavy two-shell defense with tight coverage, different from Minnesota's blitz-heavy approach. Seattle is also coming off a bye and has a rest advantage.
Raheem Morris said Seattle's system is essentially unchanged with Drew Lock, and he called Darian Price a speed and outside-zone threat the defense must set edges against.
Morris credited discipline and the five-man front, and said the safeties and corners are working well together. He said the safety rotation is based on 'the hot man will play'.

Brandin Cooks was parted with and has joined Washington. Shanahan called it a transactional move. Shanahan said a reserve returning from injury could be activated if his practices go well, given McKivitz's loss.

title: Todd Bowles: Jalen McMillan Looks ‘Fresh’ | Press Conference
headline: Jalen McMillan returned to practice and looked 'fresh', but Bowles wouldn't commit to him for Monday night vs. Carolina; Jacob Parrish did more than expected.
summary: Bowles said CB Jacob Parrish (back) did more at Wednesday's practice than he expected and will do more as the week goes on. WR Jalen McMillan returned to the field, looked fresh and healthy, and was running routes. Bowles said it's too early to say whether he can play Monday. LB Josiah Trotter is a little sore and will likely be out there later in the week. Bowles defended David Walker's snap count despite his production. Walker plays a lot, including on special teams where he is one of the team's best, and will play full time when a game calls for it. He said the 'mental part' still has to come together for that. Bowles called short-yardage failures a 'sore spot' and said the fix is scheme and blocking, not the lack of a bigger back. He expects a dogfight with Carolina, said the first meeting got out of hand early and so revealed little, and praised the Panthers' play-calling and their tight end usage, especially Tommy Tremble. Rookie CB Ayden Garnes has developed well but may stay inactive behind special-teams players, though he is in the mix to dress Monday.

injuries.detail: Practiced after a back injury and did more than Bowles expected. His workload should increase as the week goes on.
Returned to practice, looked fresh and healthy, and ran routes. Bowles said it is too early to say whether he can play Monday.
Bowles described him as a little sore and said he will probably be out there toward the later part of the week.

signals.claim: Practiced Wednesday and is being eased back in; his availability for Monday night is undecided.
signals.note: A healthy return to practice makes him a candidate to play Monday, but Bowles gave no commitment, so check the later practice reports.
signals.quote: He looked fresh. I mean he looked fresh. He looked healthy.

signals.claim: Will do more in practice as the week progresses after a back injury.
signals.note: He is trending toward playing, which helps the Tampa Bay secondary and matchups against Carolina's pass catchers.
signals.quote: he'll do more as the week progresses

signals.claim: Is sore and will likely practice later in the week.
signals.note: Minor soreness only, but his practice participation is worth watching for IDP and defensive-snap purposes.
signals.quote: he'll probably be out there toward the later of the week

signals.claim: Will keep a rotational pass-rush and special-teams role and will not move to full-time snaps unless a game requires it.
signals.note: His production is strong, but Bowles is not promising a bigger defensive snap share, which caps IDP upside.
signals.quote: He's in a good spot and he's playing right where he needs to play

signals.claim: Is in the discussion to be active Monday, but special-teams players may be prioritized.
signals.note: A rookie CB with little fantasy relevance unless injuries thin the secondary.
signals.quote: we need teams guys as well

topics.detail: Bowles called the decline in third and fourth-and-1 conversions a 'sore spot', blaming scheme and blocking. He doesn't think the lack of a bigger back is the cause.

Bowles expects a different game from the first meeting, which got out of hand early. He called it a dogfight in which turnovers and mistakes will decide the result, and said the team can't rely on the run game alone.

He praised Brad's play-calling and self-scouting, noting that the Panthers use everyone and give few tells. He said tight end Tommy Tremble is used much more than in the first meeting, alongside Waller.
Bowles said the pressure is the same every week, and that the focus is on cutting mistakes and closing out games.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cam Ward gets strong praise as a franchise QB and the offense is trending up (24+ points per game lately), but Carnell Tate's red-zone drop was called out and the defense is struggling badly.
summary: Saleh opened by saying three players were not practicing Wednesday. The names are garbled in the captions, but Terrell Burgess was one of them, and Saleh was hopeful and said they would see how the next couple of days go. He gave a positive health update on Jalen Harrell (not on the provided roster) and said the team added a long, instinctive corner who has played a couple of games for Carolina. Most of the session covered the defense, which he said has been 'bleeding' for about three weeks. He blamed hesitation and indecision against Dallas, said he will keep things simple and consistent rather than keep changing the scheme, and took responsibility for his own play-calling. On offense he said the unit is trending in the right direction and has averaged well over 24 points the last 3-4 weeks. He was very pleased with Cam Ward's development and called him the franchise quarterback. He said the red-zone problems come from penalties, turnovers and mistakes, citing a drive where Carnell Tate dropped a first-down ball at the 18 and a run-game TFL followed, and Ward could have thrown the ball away on the last drive of the half. He ended by saying the best red-zone offenses historically run the ball in. He also noted that Houston will be approached differently the second time, because the game plan builds on one extra game of film.

injuries.detail: Did not practice Wednesday. Saleh said they are hopeful and will see how the next couple of days go.
Saleh said he is in constant contact with the family and that things are trending in the right direction and getting better each day. He gave no football timeline.

Saleh said three players did not practice, but the other names are garbled in the captions. Later, about a player in his first week back, he said 'we'll continue to ramp them up' and was 'not sure if he'll be quite ready.' The player is not identifiable from the transcript.

signals.claim: Ward is the franchise quarterback and the offense will keep improving over the final seven games.
signals.note: Saleh is very positive on Ward's development and the offense's trend (24+ points per game recently), which supports his fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: he's proving that he's going to be this, this franchise, this franchise quarterback

signals.note: Saleh publicly pointed to Tate's red-zone drop as a drive-killing execution error; there is no sign of a role change.
signals.quote: Carnell drops the ball, you know, just simple things

topics.detail: Saleh said the defense has been 'bleeding' for about three weeks. In the Dallas game it looked slow to trigger and hesitant rather than just losing one-on-ones. He blamed the four-man rush, coverage on pressure calls and his own play-calling timing, but said he is confident it will improve over the last seven games.

He will not keep changing the defense after the Dallas result. The focus is on repeating techniques and fundamentals with a young group before adding anything. He used a golf-swing analogy for why constant changes don't work.
No-huddle cuts the real-time rest between defensive series from about 8-10 minutes to 4-5. Saleh said this is not an excuse for Sunday's result.

The offense has been averaging well over 24 points but needs to convert more red-zone drives into touchdowns. Saleh cited penalties, turnovers, a TFL on a run, a drop, and Ward not throwing the ball away on the final drive before half. He said the best red-zone offenses historically run the ball in or are great off-schedule teams.
The team added a corner who has played a couple of games for Carolina. Saleh described him as a big, long, instinctive corner.
Facing Houston twice in a short span means game plans built on limited film. The team will carry over plays that never got called and drop ones it didn't like. It will also add some new things.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/25/26
headline: Washington is set to sign WR Brandon Aiyuk (expected Thursday) but Quinn has no timeline for his role, and CB Amik Robertson is held out again ahead of Arizona.
summary: Quinn said the team has turned the page to Arizona and will fly out Friday night after practice. Brandon Aiyuk worked out and met with the team, and Quinn said the plan is to move forward and hopefully sign him tomorrow. Quinn praised his health, strength and explosiveness, but said Aiyuk is coming off a knee injury and hasn't played in two years. He has no timeline for when Aiyuk contributes, and said practice reps will show how quickly he gets up to speed. He pointed to learning the terminology as the first hurdle. Quinn said the team's late-game and end-of-half work has improved because of better time-management communication and not burning early timeouts. He singled out Jayden Daniels' third-and-9 scramble conversion as the key play in that drive. On injuries, Amik Robertson will be held out of practice again and isn't there yet. Rasul Douglas played almost every snap Monday and impressed Quinn. The defense is still focused on takeaways after missing chances at interceptions. Quinn is prioritizing fewer explosive plays, fewer penalties and better third-down and red-zone defense over raw yardage.

injuries.detail: Held out of practice again; Quinn said he is not there yet and will be given as much time as possible, with the next couple of days telling.
Listed as DNP for a personal matter, not an injury. Quinn didn't address his availability, only denying that Diggs tackled a teammate on purpose on Monday's final pass.

signals.claim: Will be held out of practice again today and is not yet ready to return.
signals.note: A continued absence hurts the Washington secondary's depth and makes his Arizona availability uncertain.
signals.quote: We're going to hold him today.

signals.claim: Played close to every defensive snap Monday night after previously getting only some reps.
signals.note: Quinn trusts him as a primary corner, so he's a steady defensive piece for IDP and matchup purposes.
signals.quote: going from some reps to just about all the reps

signals.note: Quinn credited his scramble conversion and his clock management for the improved two-minute offense.
signals.quote: the conversion that Jaden had on a third down and nine scramble was the one

topics.detail: Aiyuk (not on the listed roster) worked out and met with the team, and Quinn expects him to sign tomorrow. Quinn said he looked healthy, strong and explosive. Quinn described him as a contested-catch, aggressive-hands receiver and has no timeline for his on-field contribution, so this is a watch item rather than an immediate fantasy boost.
Quinn called the receiver group deep and said more injured receivers are hopefully returning before too long, without naming any.

Quinn is happy with the end-of-half and end-of-game execution of the last two weeks. The keys are communication on when to hurry or slow down and keeping timeouts in the pocket. The team will keep rehearsing it in practice.

Takeaways are the top priority after the defense finished Monday at zero and missed some interception chances. Quinn focuses on limiting explosives, penalties, third downs and red-zone scoring rather than total yards. Corners Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau were credited with experience and awareness, and a 'Mike' (likely Mike Sainristil) made a good stop on the first third down.
